sentences.en: In the previous episode of this series, we spent some time with Talisha Lee,
sentences.zh: 在本系列上一集中，我们花了一些时间陪伴塔莉莎·李（Talisha Lee），

sentences.en: a mom who was drifting between living in her car and sometimes staying with friends or family.
sentences.zh: 一位在车里生活，有时寄宿在朋友或亲戚家的母亲。

sentences.en: In that story, when Talisha finally started trying to get some help getting into housing
sentences.zh: 在那段故事里，当塔莉莎终于开始尝试寻求帮助以获得住房

sentences.en: or shelter, she began by calling 2-1-1.
sentences.zh: 或避难所时，她首先拨打了2-1-1。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for holding.
How can I assist you today?
sentences.zh: 今天有什么我可以帮您的吗？

sentences.en: Yes, me and my 11-year-old son is homeless.
sentences.zh: 是的，我和我11岁的儿子无家可归了。

sentences.en: I heard a lot about 2-1-1 doing this reporting, not just from Talisha, who called a bunch of times,
sentences.zh: 在做这篇报道时，我听到了很多关于2-1-1的评价，不仅来自打过很多次电话的塔莉莎，

sentences.en: but from everyone, from homeless people and service providers and advocates.
sentences.zh: 还来自所有人，包括无家可归者、服务提供者和倡导者。

sentences.en: It seemed like 2-1-1 was almost always the starting place for people who were looking for help.
sentences.zh: 对于寻求帮助的人来说，2-1-1似乎总是他们的起点。

sentences.en: But mostly, when people talked about calling, they were frustrated.
sentences.zh: 但大多数时候，当人们谈到拨打这个电话时，他们感到很沮丧。

sentences.en: They'd say, I called, but it didn't work, or I called, but I didn't get anything.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我打过电话，但没用，或者我打过电话，但什么也没得到。

sentences.en: In her mind, 2-1-1 and the system were the same thing, and they hadn't come through for her.
sentences.zh: 在她看来，2-1-1和整个系统是一回事，而它们并没有为她提供实质性的帮助。

sentences.en: So, what was 2-1-1's role in the system that helps people out of homelessness?
sentences.zh: 那么，2-1-1在帮助人们摆脱无家可归的系统中扮演什么角色呢？

sentences.en: And why did it seem like a dead end for so many people?
sentences.zh: 为什么对许多人来说，它似乎是一条死胡同？

sentences.en: At the beginning of March, right before everything shut down for the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 三月初，就在一切因疫情而关闭之前，

sentences.en: I paid a visit to the 2-1-1 call center.
I found answers to those questions.
sentences.zh: 我找到了这些问题的答案。

sentences.en: But I also found a whole fascinating world, where the boundaries that separate caller and operator are blurrier than I imagined.
sentences.zh: 但我也发现了一个迷人的世界，在那里，来电者和接线员之间的界限比我想象的要模糊得多。

sentences.en: In Alameda County, 2-1-1 is run by a non-profit called Eden INR, and is located in the city of Hayward, southeast of Oakland.
sentences.zh: 在阿拉米达县（Alameda County），2-1-1由一家名为Eden INR的非营利组织运营，位于奥克兰东南部的海沃德市（Hayward）。

sentences.en: The main call center room is about the size of an elementary school classroom.
sentences.zh: 主要的呼叫中心房间大约有一个小学教室那么大。

sentences.en: It has brown carpet, fluorescent lighting, and non-profit energy.
sentences.zh: 里面铺着棕色的地毯，有荧光灯，充满了非营利组织特有的氛围。

sentences.en: Thank you for letting me sit in on your work today.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天让我旁听您的工作。

sentences.en: There's a little coffee station and a mini fridge, and seven operators at desks, all wearing headsets.
sentences.zh: 那里有一个小咖啡台和一个迷你冰箱，七名接线员坐在办公桌前，都戴着耳机。

sentences.en: As the day goes on, there will be moments when they are all talking at once.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，会有他们所有人同时在通话的时刻。

sentences.en: You need to call them between 7 p.m., Monday to Friday.
sentences.zh: 你需要周一到周五的晚上7点之间给他们打电话。

sentences.en: Not all of the people who call 2-1-1 are homeless, but most of them are low income.
sentences.zh: 并非所有拨打2-1-1的人都无家可归，但他们大多数都是低收入者。

sentences.en: It could be just having a crisis going on.
sentences.zh: 可能只是因为正处于某种危机之中。

sentences.en: You know, the ends are not meeting for this month.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这个月入不敷出了。

sentences.en: The ends are not going to meet for the next few months, or someone's had an injury on the job.
sentences.zh: 接下来的几个月也入不敷出，或者有人在工作中受了伤。

sentences.en: That's an operator named Roshana Robinson.
sentences.zh: 那是名叫罗莎娜·罗宾逊（Roshana Robinson）的接线员。

sentences.en: And she says, people call 2-1-1 looking for help paying their electric bill and help paying rent.
sentences.zh: 她说，人们拨打2-1-1是为了寻求支付电费和房租的帮助。

sentences.en: Help doing all kinds of things that money can solve, if you've got it.
sentences.zh: 寻求各种只要有钱就能解决的问题的帮助。

sentences.en: I'm calling me the county of 2-1-1.
I'm not going to help you.
Just a note here, any callers you hear in this episode have given us their explicit permission to play their call.
sentences.zh: 这里说明一下，本集中您听到的任何来电者都已明确许可我们播放他们的通话录音。

sentences.en: Although, in some cases, we've taken out their names.
sentences.zh: 尽管在某些情况下，我们隐去了他们的名字。

sentences.en: I would like to know, do y'all know anybody that give a washing machine?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你们有人知道谁能提供洗衣机吗？

sentences.en: One 93-year-old woman who called while I was there said last time she walked to the laundromat, she nearly fainted from exhaustion.
sentences.zh: 一位在我参观时打进电话的93岁老妇人说，上次她走到自助洗衣店时，差点因为精疲力竭而晕倒。

sentences.en: She calls Roshana baby, and sometimes sir, which Roshana is completely unfazed by.
sentences.zh: 她管罗莎娜叫“宝贝”，有时叫“先生”，罗莎娜对此完全不为所动。

sentences.en: The vast web of government services and nonprofits can be hard to navigate, especially for people who may not have the internet at home.
sentences.zh: 庞大的政府服务和非营利组织网络可能很难驾驭，特别是对于家里可能没有互联网的人来说。

sentences.en: 2-1-1 operators are trying to point callers toward resources that might benefit them, which is why they're officially called phone resource specialists.
sentences.zh: 2-1-1接线员试图引导来电者寻找可能对他们有益的资源，这就是为什么他们正式的称呼是“电话资源专员”。

sentences.en: But with their blessing, I'm going to stick with the less jargony term, operator.
sentences.zh: 但在他们的许可下，我还是沿用那个不那么专业的术语：接线员。

sentences.en: Can I just, like, record a little bit while you do the shelter calls?
sentences.zh: 我能录一点你们打避难所电话的过程吗？

sentences.en: Early in the day, Jada Gonzalez, one of the operators, starts calling shelters in Alameda County to see if they have space available.
sentences.zh: 当天早些时候，接线员之一的杰达·冈萨雷斯（Jada Gonzalez）开始拨打阿拉米达县的避难所电话，看看是否有空位。
只是想查询一下避难所的空位。

sentences.en: Jada's been an operator at 2-1-1 for seven years, and she's done these calls so many times that the words come out quick and tonal, almost divorced from meaning.
sentences.zh: 杰达在2-1-1做接线员已经七年了，她打这些电话打得太多了，以至于说出来的话语调平稳、语速极快，几乎脱离了原本的含义。
只是想查询一下避难所的空位。

sentences.en: Well, we do have resources for deposit assistance.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们确实有押金援助方面的资源。

sentences.en: A lot of people who call 2-1-1 are looking for shelter, and if there are spaces available, the operators can help reserve them a bed.
sentences.zh: 许多拨打2-1-1的人都在寻找避难所，如果有空位，接线员可以帮他们预留床位。

sentences.en: But keeping track of an inventory of shelter beds is more challenging than you might imagine.
sentences.zh: 但要追踪避难所床位的库存比你想象的要困难得多。

sentences.en: The number of open beds is always in flux.
sentences.zh: 空余床位的数量总是在变动。

sentences.en: There are shelters that have 80 beds in the winter and 60 in the summer, and beds that just suddenly pop up in some random church basement.
sentences.zh: 有的避难所在冬天有80个床位，夏天只有60个，还有些床位会突然出现在某个随机的教堂地下室里。

sentences.en: There are separate shelters reserved for victims of domestic violence.
sentences.zh: 还有专门为家庭暴力受害者预留的独立避难所。

sentences.en: There are shelters that take moms with their kids if the kids are under 10, but not over 10.
sentences.zh: 有的避难所接收带孩子的母亲，前提是孩子在10岁以下，超过10岁就不行。

sentences.en: There are currently no shelters in the county that accept fathers with their kids, but there might be one opening soon.
sentences.zh: 目前县里还没有避难所接收带孩子的父亲，但可能很快会开一家。

sentences.en: Jada calls a few more shelters with the same results.
sentences.zh: 杰达又打了几个避难所的电话，结果都一样。

sentences.en: So far today, all they have to offer callers is one spot for a mother and two children.
sentences.zh: 到今天为止，他们能提供给来电者的只有一个供一位母亲和两个孩子使用的名额。

sentences.en: Roshana told me she got a call recently from a mother who needed shelter for that night, and she had nothing to give her.
sentences.zh: 罗莎娜告诉我，她最近接到一位母亲的电话，对方需要当晚的避难所，但她什么也提供不了。

sentences.en: It was on the phone with me.
What do I got to do?
She's like, so, me and my child were literally about to be on the streets the night.
sentences.zh: 她说，我和我的孩子今晚真的要流落街头了。

sentences.en: I wanted to go by her a hotel room.
sentences.zh: 我当时真想去给她开个酒店房间。

sentences.en: I was on the phone with her for 33 minutes, and she was, I know she was staying on the phone with me to think I was going to give her, like, her light of hope.
sentences.zh: 我和她通了33分钟电话，我知道她一直不挂断是以为我会给她一线希望。

sentences.en: And I was hopeless to her.
sentences.zh: 而我对她来说却无能为力。

sentences.en: Already I was starting to understand why people were always saying, I called 2-1-1 and I didn't get anything.
sentences.zh: 我已经开始明白为什么人们总是说，我打过2-1-1，但什么也没得到。

sentences.en: They weren't getting anything, because there was nothing to give.
sentences.zh: 他们什么也没得到，因为确实没什么可给的。

sentences.en: Thank you for calling Alameda County 2-1-1.
sentences.zh: 感谢您拨打阿拉米达县2-1-1。
有什么我可以帮您的吗？

sentences.en: Homeless callers who want help with something other than shelter, like housing, for example, will have to get into the county's coordinated entry system.
sentences.zh: 想要寻求避难所以外帮助（例如住房）的无家可归者，必须进入县里的协调准入系统。

sentences.en: And this, this was the same system Talisha had entered.
sentences.zh: 而这，正是塔莉莎曾经进入过的同一个系统。

sentences.en: 2-1-1, it turns out, is sort of like a doorman for this system, opening the door for some people to enter, but not for others.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，2-1-1就像是这个系统的门卫，为一些人打开进入的大门，但对另一些人则不然。

sentences.en: Okay, and you're looking for housing?
sentences.zh: 好的，您是在寻找住房吗？

sentences.en: Around 10 a.m., I get to see one of these calls.
sentences.zh: 大约上午10点，我得以旁听了其中一个电话。

sentences.en: An operator named Gupreet Minhas gets a call from a 24-year-old mother who wants help with housing.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫古普里特·明哈斯（Gupreet Minhas）的接线员接到了一位24岁母亲的电话，她想寻求住房方面的帮助。

sentences.en: To get that help, she'll need to go into the coordinated entry system.
sentences.zh: 要获得那种帮助，她需要进入协调准入系统。

sentences.en: But whether she makes it in at all depends, essentially, on how she answers one question.
sentences.zh: 但她能否成功进入，本质上取决于她如何回答一个问题。

sentences.en: And where did you guys sleep or stay last night?
sentences.zh: 你们昨晚是在哪里睡觉或留宿的？

sentences.en: Gupreet is screening this caller to determine if she meets the definition of literal homelessness,
sentences.zh: 古普里特正在筛选这位来电者，以确定她是否符合“字面意义上的无家可归”的定义，

sentences.en: according to the Department of Housing and Urban Development, and by extension, Alameda County.
sentences.zh: 根据住房和城市发展部的规定，以及阿拉米达县的延伸规定。

sentences.en: That's the actual term they use, literal homelessness.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们使用的确切术语：字面意义上的无家可归。

sentences.en: You are literally homeless if last night you slept in a shelter or in a place not meant for human habitation,
sentences.zh: 如果你昨晚睡在避难所，或者睡在不适合人类居住的地方，那你就是字面意义上的无家可归，

sentences.en: like a tent or a car or a broken-down RV.
sentences.zh: 比如帐篷、汽车或报废的房车。

sentences.en: If this is the case, then you get the rubber stamp of literal homelessness,
sentences.zh: 如果是这种情况，你就会获得“字面意义上的无家可归”的盖章认证，

sentences.en: and the operators can pass you along to do a longer interview,
sentences.zh: 接线员就可以把你转介去进行更长时间的访谈，

sentences.en: in which you'll be asked a bunch more questions about your particular situation
sentences.zh: 在访谈中，你会被问到更多关于你具体情况的问题，

sentences.en: and then entered into the system.
But here's the kind of maddening thing.
sentences.zh: 但这里有一件令人抓狂的事情。

sentences.en: Say you stay in the car for three months,
sentences.zh: 假设你在车里住了三个月，

sentences.en: and then one day you sleep at a friend's house,
sentences.zh: 然后有一天你睡在朋友家，

sentences.en: but that's the day you happen to call 2-1-1.
sentences.zh: 而偏偏就在那天你拨打了2-1-1。

sentences.en: In that case, you're not literally homeless, according to their definition.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，根据他们的定义，你就不属于字面意义上的无家可归。

sentences.en: And if you're not literally homeless, you can't get into the system at all,
sentences.zh: 如果你不属于字面意义上的无家可归，你就根本无法进入系统，

sentences.en: which means you can't get help with housing.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你无法获得住房方面的帮助。

sentences.en: And this caller that Gupreet is talking to, she seems to realize this.
sentences.zh: 而古普里特正在交谈的这位来电者，似乎意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: We don't have permission from her to play the recording,
sentences.zh: 我们没有得到她播放录音的许可，

sentences.en: so I'll paraphrase what's happening on her end.
sentences.zh: 所以我将转述她那边发生的情况。

sentences.en: In response to Gupreet's question about where she slept last night,
sentences.zh: 针对古普里特关于她昨晚睡在哪里的问题，

sentences.en: someone told me that I should tell you I've been sleeping in my car.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉我，我应该告诉你们我一直睡在车里。

sentences.en: It's not what somebody told you, it's just, where did you sleep last night?
sentences.zh: 这不是别人告诉你的问题，只是，你昨晚睡在哪里？

sentences.en: well, my kids don't sleep in the car, but I do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的孩子们不睡在车里，但我睡。

sentences.en: So last night, where did you sleep?
Did you sleep in the car?
Did you sleep on the street?
Did you sleep in someone's home?
sentences.zh: 你睡在某人的家里了吗？
我在借宿别人的沙发，她说，

sentences.en: but when there's no room, I go to my car.
sentences.zh: 但当没有地方住的时候，我就去车里。

sentences.en: Okay, so question again, where were you last night?
sentences.zh: 好的，再次问一下，你昨晚在哪里？

sentences.en: Where did you sleep last night?
In my car, in my car.
sentences.zh: 在我的车里，在我的车里。

sentences.en: How long have you been sleeping in your car?
I feel like you guys want a straightforward answer,
sentences.zh: 我觉得你们想要一个直截了当的回答，

sentences.en: but I can't give you one.
It's pretty simple questions, ma'am, and...
sentences.zh: 女士，这些问题很简单，而且……

sentences.en: This caller's situation is complicated and in flux,
sentences.zh: 这位来电者的情况很复杂，而且处于变动中，

sentences.en: but Gapreet needs to check a box.
sentences.zh: 但加普里特（Gapreet）需要勾选一个选项。

sentences.en: Give me one second, I'm going to put you on hold,
sentences.zh: 请稍等，我要把你转入保留状态，

sentences.en: and I'll see if I can get them on the other line, okay?
sentences.zh: 我去看看能不能接通另一条线，好吗？
加普里特还是把她转接了过去，

sentences.en: even though it feels unclear to her
whether the woman fulfills the criteria or not.
sentences.zh: 这位女士是否符合条件。
更深入的访谈可能会揭示，

sentences.en: that she doesn't need the definition

sentences.zh: 字面意义上的无家可归的定义。

sentences.en: She wants to say she's literally homeless,
sentences.zh: 她想说自己是字面意义上的无家可归，

sentences.en: but I think she's actually been staying at a friend's house,
sentences.zh: 但我认为她实际上一直住在朋友家，

sentences.en: where she's going to end up saying that.
And then what they're trying to help with this program
is individuals who don't have any other resources.
sentences.zh: 是那些没有任何其他资源的人。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems like part of what she was getting hung up on
sentences.zh: 我是说，她纠结的部分原因似乎在于，

sentences.en: is that the questions sort of didn't account for, like, nuance.
sentences.zh: 这些问题没有考虑到细微差别。

sentences.en: And I understand we need to be more, you know, more patient,
sentences.zh: 我明白我们需要更，你知道，更有耐心，

sentences.en: but sometimes it's just so difficult
because they're just, like, constantly, like, attacking you
sentences.zh: 因为他们一直在，就像，不断地攻击你，

sentences.en: and you're just asking them simple questions,
sentences.zh: 而你只是在问他们简单的问题，

sentences.en: but it's just, so, it's like a struggle.
sentences.zh: 但这真的，太难了，就像一场挣扎。

sentences.en: When Talisha Lee called 2-1-1 in the last episode,
sentences.zh: 当塔莉莎·李（Talisha Lee）在上集拨打2-1-1时，

sentences.en: she could truthfully say she was sleeping in her car at the time,
sentences.zh: 她可以如实说当时睡在车里，

sentences.en: which meant she was ultimately allowed to enter the system.
sentences.zh: 这意味着她最终被允许进入系统。

sentences.en: But hers was a similarly influx situation.
sentences.zh: 但她的情况也同样处于变动中。

sentences.en: She was often drifting between sleeping in the car
and sleeping on someone's floor or couch.
sentences.zh: 和睡在别人的地板或沙发上之间徘徊。

sentences.en: Staying with other people like that in a temporary, unstable way
sentences.zh: 像这样以一种临时、不稳定的方式与他人同住，

sentences.en: is often referred to as being doubled up.
that there were about 220,000 students in California
who were living doubled up in 2018.
That's 220,000 kids plus their parents or guardians
sentences.zh: 那是22万名孩子加上他们的父母或监护人，

sentences.en: that HUD may not be counting as homeless,
sentences.zh: 住房和城市发展部（HUD）可能并未将他们计为无家可归者，

sentences.en: who do not, in fact, have homes.
sentences.zh: 而他们实际上确实没有家。

sentences.en: they're told they're not literally homeless.
sentences.zh: 他们被告知自己并非字面意义上的无家可归。

sentences.en: People really get frustrated when you tell them

sentences.zh: 自己不是字面意义上的无家可归时，真的会很沮丧，

sentences.en: and they're like, I am homeless.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我就是无家可归啊。

sentences.en: I'm sleeping on the effing couch,
and I'm sleeping in my effing car,
and I just got let in last night.
sentences.zh: 而且我昨晚才刚被赶出来。

sentences.en: But even when people do make it
sentences.zh: 但即使人们成功进入了
